compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`make amend-msg` exists because `git commit --amend -F/-m` REPLACES the whole message and so
silently drops the `Change-Id` trailer. It carries the `Change-Id` forward correctly — and then
drops `Signed-off-by` by the same mechanism it was built to prevent.

`scripts/amend_commit_message.py`:

```python
def compose_message(new_message: str, change_id: str) -> str:
    return _git_stdout("interpret-trailers", "--trailer", f"Change-Id: {change_id}",
                       stdin=strip_change_id_lines(new_message))

def amend_head(message: str) -> int:
    ...
    ["git", "commit", "--amend", "--file", str(tmp)]
```

Only `Change-Id` is read off HEAD and re-attached. Everything else comes from `FILE`, and
`--file` replaces the message wholesale — so a `Signed-off-by` present on HEAD but absent from
the author's new message file is gone.

Observed: an agent rewriting a commit message with `make amend-msg` lost its `Signed-off-by`
while the `Change-Id` survived. It noticed only because it happened to re-inspect the trailers,
and restored it with `git commit --amend --no-edit -s`.

## Why this is a defect and not a usage error

The tool's own docstring anticipates the trailer block containing `Signed-off-by` — it is named
as the neighbour `interpret-trailers` appends next to. So the code knows the trailer is there
and preserves only its sibling.

More to the point, the wrapper's stated rationale applies verbatim to the trailer it drops. From
the Makefile target:

> `git commit --amend -F/-m` REPLACES the whole message, dropping the Change-Id … No hook can
> catch it … the remedy is a wrapper that makes the failure unreachable.

Same argument, same file, same failure mode, other mandatory trailer. The wrapper makes one
failure unreachable and leaves the other reachable through itself.

## The loss is silent — nothing catches it

- No CI job asserts a commit HAS a `Signed-off-by`. `scripts/check_dco_identity.py` is a
  different check: it scans **docs** for hardcoded personal sign-off identities.
- `scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py` treats `Signed-off-by:` as a trailer for wrapping
  purposes only; it does not require one.
- The `commit-msg` hook stamps `Change-Id`, not sign-off.

So the amend succeeds, looks correct, and the missing DCO attestation surfaces later or not at
all. CONTRIBUTING.md requires the sign-off; the sanctioned tool for rewriting a message removes
it without saying so.

## Scope

Carry `Signed-off-by` forward from HEAD the same way `Change-Id` already is, when the new
message does not supply one. Preserve existing behaviour when the author's file DOES include a
sign-off — including multiple sign-offs, which are legitimate — and do not duplicate it.

Explicitly OUT of scope: adding a CI gate that requires sign-off on every commit. That is a
separate, larger policy decision about enforcement; this ticket is only that the tool must not
silently destroy a trailer that was already there. Also out of scope: changing which identity
signs, or `check_dco_identity.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Amending with a message file that omits `Signed-off-by` preserves HEAD's existing
      sign-off — verified by a test asserting the trailer survives the amend
- [ ] A message file that DOES carry a sign-off is respected and the trailer is not duplicated —
      verified by a test
- [ ] Multiple distinct `Signed-off-by` trailers on HEAD all survive — verified by a test
- [ ] `Change-Id` carry-forward is unchanged, including the existing refusal when HEAD has none
      — verified by the existing tests continuing to pass unmodified
compiled_state.title: make amend-msg drops Signed-off-by, the same silent trailer loss it was built to prevent for Change-Id
